doc.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

title: Fats Waller and Carmen McRae liner notes, Strayhorn and Kenny Clarke
summary: Sorting out which liner notes held the Waller story; the Carmen McRae Decca date, Billy Strayhorn, and Kenny Clarke hiring him.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I’ve got to remember that Fats Waller story, which album I wrote it in, because I don’t know if it was Carmen’s or not and it’s bugging me what it was. Because what would be the connection. Okay. Boing, the bell went on. I wrote the notes to — Orrin Keepnews who was my partner in Milestone Records gave me a certain amount of work when he started doing all these reissues. And one of the assignments was not too many years ago in the 90s, was a Fats Waller compilation, which was fun, because I loved all that. So in the introduction to those notes, I told the Fats Waller story when I was a kid about going down in the basement, that’s where it comes from, in the Royal Theater and all of that. So it’s not Carmen McRae. Because what I told in the Carmen notes was my experiences with her at Minton’s. And how I came to play there and the whole thing with her and when I went to make the album for Decca there was a little guy with glasses sitting in the audience who turned out to be Billy Strayhorn. And he came up and played “Something to Live For” for her. And you know who hired me for that record? Kenny Clarke? I was working with him at the Bohemia at the time. Interestingly, not too many years before
that he was married to Carmen, so there he was leading this date for her so they became friends I guess eventually.
